review_notes: I read the whole target file and its supporting file CompactWordCost.lean. I also read the isCompact_set_pow lemma in CompactGeneratingBalls.lean. I looked for specialised hypotheses throughout. The bounded-metric hypothesis `hbounded` looks specialised, but generalising it to a constant would need new mathematics, so I did not report it. The one clear case is `[IsTopologicalGroup G]` in `weightedGroupMetric_proper`, where `[ContinuousMul G]` is enough. I did not compile the replacement. Instance resolution should work because `IsTopologicalGroup` extends `ContinuousMul`, but that is unchecked. The topology instance on G comes from the ambient MetricSpace, so `[ContinuousMul G]` refers to that topology.

findings.problem: The statement assumes `IsTopologicalGroup G`, but the proof only needs continuity of multiplication. The two uses of the hypothesis are `isCompact_set_pow K hcompact n` and `continuous_const.mul continuous_id`. `isCompact_set_pow` is stated for `[TopologicalSpace G] [ContinuousMul G]`. The rest of the proof uses only metric facts and lemmas already in this file. Inverse continuity is never used, so the assumption is stronger than necessary.
findings.proposed_change: Change the binder to `theorem weightedGroupMetric_proper [ContinuousMul G] (hcompact : IsCompact K) : ...`. The proof body stays the same. `isCompact_set_pow` accepts `[ContinuousMul G]` directly. `continuous_const.mul continuous_id` needs only `ContinuousMul`. `IsTopologicalGroup` extends `ContinuousMul`, so existing callers that supply an `IsTopologicalGroup` instance still elaborate.
findings.benefit: The properness result then applies to topological monoid-like settings, such as groups whose metric is left-invariant but whose inversion is not known to be continuous. It also states exactly which structure the argument uses.
